s.n: Egg quota curried egg and cress sandwiches
s.note: the eggs the chickens have to lay to stay alive
s.how: Boil 6 eggs for 9 minutes, cool in iced water and peel. Mash with 4 tbsp mayo, half a tsp mild curry powder, chopped chives, salt and white pepper. Butter 8 slices soft white bread and spread the egg over 4. Scatter with a punnet of cress, close, cut off the crusts and cut each into 4 triangles.

Brush 2 sheets puff pastry with beaten egg and cover one with 80g grated parmesan and a pinch of paprika. Lay the other on top, press, cut into strips and twist. Bake at 200C for 12 minutes until golden and crisp.

m.n: Pie machine beef and onion pies
m.note: Mrs Tweedy's pie machine, beef only
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 2 sliced onions, thyme, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp Worcestershire and 500ml beef stock, cover and braise for 2.5 hours. Thicken with 2 tbsp cornflour in water and cool. Line 4 pie tins with shortcrust, fill, top with puff, egg wash and bake at 200C for 30 minutes. Simmer 300g frozen peas with butter and mash roughly.

w.note: a proper British pudding for the flight
w.how: Rub 100g butter into 250g self-raising flour, then add 150ml cold water to a soft dough. Roll to a rectangle, spread with 150g raspberry jam and roll up. Wrap loosely in baking paper and foil and bake at 180C for 40 minutes. Serve with custard.

d.n: Coop meeting honey malt hot chocolate
d.note: the hens' late-night meetings in the hut
d.how: Warm 1L milk in a saucepan until steaming but not boiling. Whisk in 3 tbsp cocoa, 4 tbsp malted milk powder and 2 tbsp honey until smooth and frothy. Pour into four mugs, top each with a spoonful of whipped cream and grate a little dark chocolate over the top.
